variables.meaning: a vector, an n-tuple (x₁, x₂, …, xₙ) of real numbers written as a column, drawn as an arrow with a direction and a magnitude
a second vector, added to or subtracted from x⃗, or the vector a mapping returns
a unit vector, a vector of magnitude one giving a direction
the standard basis vectors e⃗₁, …, e⃗ₙ of ℝⁿ, each with a single 1 and zeros elsewhere
a mapping F: ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ that takes a vector x⃗ to a vector F(x⃗), linear when it respects sums and scalar multiples
an m × n matrix, an array of m rows and n columns, which as a linear mapping takes e⃗_j to its jth column
the 2 × 2 matrix [1 2; 3 4] of the worked example, as a linear mapping of the plane
the entry of a matrix in row i and column j
a linear differential operator, a linear mapping of an infinite-dimensional space of functions, L f = g
an m × n matrix, a linear mapping from ℝⁿ to ℝᵐ, added to, scaled, multiplied, inverted or transposed
a second matrix, of the same size as A for a sum and of size n × p for the product AB
a third matrix in the rules of matrix algebra
a column vector the matrices act on
a second column vector in the dot product x⃗ · y⃗ = y⃗ᵀx⃗
the columns b⃗₁, …, b⃗_p of the matrix B, each carried by A to a column of AB
the identity matrix, 1s on the main diagonal and zeros elsewhere, I_n for the n × n one
the inverse of A, the matrix with AA⁻¹ = I = A⁻¹A
the transpose of A, rows and columns swapped
the coefficient matrix of a system of linear equations Ax⃗ = b⃗, or any matrix put through elimination
the vector of unknowns x₁, …, xₙ of a linear system, or a vector in a linear combination
the right-hand side of the system Ax⃗ = b⃗
the zero vector, the right-hand side of a homogeneous equation Ax⃗ = 0⃗
the vectors y⃗₁, …, y⃗ₙ of a linear combination, or the combination y⃗ = α₁x⃗₁ + ⋯ + αₙx⃗ₙ
the column vectors v⃗₁, …, v⃗₄ from which a linearly independent subset is picked
the standard basis vectors, the columns of I, the right-hand sides solved for to find the columns of A⁻¹
the identity matrix, written beside A in the augmented matrix [A | I]
the inverse of A, read off the reduced row echelon form [I | A⁻¹]
the transpose of A, whose rank equals that of A
a matrix whose kernel, the set of solutions of Lx⃗ = 0⃗, is studied; in reduced row echelon form in the examples
a subspace of ℝⁿ, a set of vectors closed under addition and scalar multiplication
the vectors v⃗₁, …, v⃗ₖ of a basis of a subspace
a vector of the subspace S, uniquely represented in its basis
a vector of a subspace, or the unknown of Lx⃗ = 0⃗ or Ax⃗ = b⃗
a second vector of a subspace, added to x⃗
the zero vector, the only member of the trivial subspace
a matrix whose column space, row space, rank and nullity are found
the right-hand side of Ax⃗ = b⃗ in the Fredholm alternative
a vector in an inner product, or the vector expressed in an orthogonal basis or projected onto a subspace
the second vector of an inner product ⟨x⃗, y⃗⟩
a third vector in the distributive rules of the inner product
the nonzero vector projected onto, or the vectors v⃗₁, …, v⃗ₙ of an orthogonal basis
the vector projected onto v⃗, or the orthogonal vectors w⃗₁, …, w⃗ₙ the Gram–Schmidt process builds
a multiple of v⃗; the projection is the one closest to w⃗
the orthogonal projection proj_v⃗(w⃗) of w⃗ onto v⃗, or proj_S(x⃗) onto a subspace
the angle between two vectors based at the same point, 0 ≤ θ ≤ π, from cos θ = ⟨x⃗, y⃗⟩/(‖x⃗‖‖y⃗‖)
a subspace spanned by an orthogonal basis, onto which a vector is projected
a square matrix whose determinant is defined, or the 2 × 2 matrix [1 1; −1 1] mapping the unit square
a second square matrix in det(AB) = det(A)det(B)
the matrix A with its ith row and jth column deleted, whose determinant enters the cofactor expansion
the entry of A in row i and column j, multiplying the cofactor (−1)^(i+j) det(A_ij)
the identity matrix, with det(I) = 1
the inverse of A, with det(A⁻¹) = 1/det(A)
the transpose of A, with det(Aᵀ) = det(A)
